Subject: Pricing exhibit questions and a couple of redlines

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the call earlier — attached is our annotated pricing exhibit. A few items jumped out on our side and I wanted to put them in writing so procurement can track:

- The proposed monthly minimum (the “floor”) reads as a hard gating metric rather than a smoothing target. For a healthcare deployment we need a 3-month smoothing/true-up window rather than an immediate termination or penalty.
- The escalation paragraph references CPI — we can’t accept an open CPI peg; can you propose a fixed-step annual escalation instead (e.g., +2.5% on the anniversary)?
- The emergency burst credits language isn’t clear whether credits are billable when used beyond burst. We need explicit language that burst overage will be billed at the listed overage rate with a one-time waiver for onboarding months.

Attachment: BluePeak_Pricing_Exhibit_Markup.pdf (pdf, 1 page, comments inline)

Would you be able to send any alternative wording you’d accept? If it helps I’m available for a 30m working session tomorrow morning.

Best,

Sarah Turner

Sarah — thanks for the markup and clear asks. Appreciate the detail.

Quick response while I loop in Legal (Laura) and Sales (Ben):

1) Smoothing/true-up: we’re comfortable adding a three-month rolling true-up for the floor. Operationally this would mean: if actual usage is below the floor in month N, BluePeak may true-up deficits across months N+1 and N+2 before any fee adjustments or penalties kick in. We’ll also add a one-time onboarding carveout for months 0–2.

2) CPI escalation swap: happy to replace CPI with a fixed annual step. Our starting proposal: fixed +2.5% on each renewal anniversary, capped at +5% over any consecutive two-year period. Open to negotiating the cap.

3) Burst credits: agree that onboarding should include a one-time waiver for first-month bursts. After that, overage billed at the stated overage rate in Exhibit B; we can add explicit language and an example calculation to avoid confusion.

I’ve attached a short note with proposed clause language and examples. If this looks OK to you I’ll ask Laura to incorporate clean redline language into the order form. Otherwise let’s take the 30m slot and finalize.

Looping in a quick sales take and proposed compromise language for legal to consider.

- On the mid-course review: propose a failsafe that either party can trigger a review at the end of the third month following go-live if the rolling average deviates more than 40% from the agreed floor. If both parties agree, the floor may be adjusted prospectively (not retroactively).

- On escalation: accept +2.5% fixed step; counter-proposal: hard cap at +3% per year and an aggregate cap of +6% across any rolling 24-month window. That preserves predictability for both sides.

Suggested contract text (for insertion into Exhibit B):
"
Capacity Floor Smoothing: Customer will be subject to a three-month rolling true-up for the Capacity Minimum described in Exhibit B. If actual usage for any rolling three-month period is consistently below fifty percent (50%) of the Capacity Minimum, either party may request a mid-course review to re-assess the Capacity Minimum. Any adjustment will be prospective and documented via an amendment to the applicable Order Form.

Annual Escalation: On each anniversary of the Effective Date, fees listed in Exhibit B will increase by two point five percent (2.5%). Such increases will not exceed three percent (3.0%) in any single twelve-month period and will not exceed six percent (6.0%) across any consecutive twenty-four month period.
"

If Legal (Laura) is OK we can push this back to Sarah and procurement — it keeps our economics intact while giving BluePeak predictability.

—Ben

Thanks everyone — I reviewed Ben’s suggested text and Sarah’s redlines. Below are proposed clean-order-form clauses that legal is comfortable shipping to the customer. I’ve embedded the operative language and flagged two small open items (both commercial, not legal).

Proposed operative language to replace current Exhibit B clauses:

1) Capacity Floor Smoothing (operative clause):
Customer will be subject to a three-month rolling true-up for the Capacity Minimum set forth in Exhibit B. If actual usage for any rolling three-month period is consistently below fifty percent (50%) of the Capacity Minimum, either party may request a mid-course review to re-assess the Capacity Minimum. Any adjustment agreed by the parties will be prospective and memorialized in an amendment to the applicable Order Form. The parties will undertake a mutual review at the end of Month 3 following Go-Live to confirm whether the Capacity Minimum should remain in effect.

2) Annual Escalation (operative clause):
On each anniversary of the Effective Date, fees listed in Exhibit B will increase by two point five percent (2.5%). In no event will such increase exceed three percent (3.0%) in any single twelve-month period or six percent (6.0%) across any consecutive twenty-four (24) month period.

3) Burst Overage and Onboarding Waiver (operative clause):
Redwood will provide a one-time onboarding waiver for burst usage incurred in the first two (2) months following Go-Live. Thereafter, any burst usage beyond the Capacity Minimum will be billed at the overage rate specified in Exhibit B. For clarity, Exhibit B will include an illustrative calculation example showing the overage calculation and invoice presentation.

Open items for commercial confirmation (please advise):
- BluePeak asked for an explicit negative-balancing protection if usage is >50% below floor for a sustained period — Legal agrees to the mid-course review language above, but we need Sales/Finance to confirm whether we will accept a prospective downward adjustment without any fee recovery for the prior period.
- The customer requested a firm +2.5% with a +3% per-year hard cap; I’ve implemented that. Sales to confirm aggregate cap (+6% over 24 months) is acceptable — Ben’s text has that.

Attachments: orderform_exhibit_clean_v2.docx (docx, 3 pages), pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet)
